cohort: The study included 165 primiparous pregnant women referred to the prenatal clinic in Tehran, Iran.
finding: Prenatal education, delivered either via social media or in-person, significantly increased vaginal birth preference and reduced elective cesarean section rates compared to a control group, although it did not significantly impact pregnancy experience or fear of childbirth.
mod_finding: Both social media-based and in-person prenatal education interventions resulted in higher rates of vaginal birth and significantly lower rates of elective cesarean sections compared to the control group.
